title: The Holiday Blues, with Elaine Rodino, PhD

sentences.en: Do you feel anxious when Christmas lights start appearing in your neighborhood every year?
sentences.zh: 你是否每年看到社区里挂起圣诞彩灯时，就会感到焦虑？

sentences.en: You're not alone.
sentences.zh: 你并不孤单。

sentences.en: For some people, the holiday season brings with it not joy and cheer, but stress, loneliness, and sadness.
sentences.zh: 对有些人来说，节日季带来的不是欢乐与喜庆，而是压力、孤独和悲伤。

sentences.en: For others, the holidays are a happy time spent reconnecting with family near and far, sharing great meals, engaging in cherished traditions.
sentences.zh: 对另一些人来说，节日是一段快乐的时光，可以与远近的亲人重新建立联系，共享丰盛的大餐，并参与珍视的传统。

sentences.en: But not this year.
sentences.zh: 但今年可不一样。

sentences.en: This strange year, nothing about the holidays will be normal, as many of us will be forgoing family visits, holiday parties, and other traditions.
sentences.zh: 在这个奇怪的年份，节日的一切都不会恢复正常，因为我们中的许多人将无法与家人团聚、参加节日派对以及进行其他传统活动。

sentences.en: For some people, these changes will be hard to take.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，这些变化将很难接受。

sentences.en: For others, they might be a welcome relief.
sentences.zh: 对另一些人来说，这可能是一种受欢迎的解脱。

sentences.en: I'm talking about the holiday blues.
sentences.zh: 我说的就是节日忧郁症。

sentences.en: You've probably heard the term, and while there's no formal diagnosis of holiday blues, these feelings are quite real for some people.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过这个词，虽然对节日忧郁症并没有正式的诊断，但这种感受对某些人来说确实真实存在。

sentences.en: What exactly are the holiday blues?
sentences.zh: 究竟什么是节日忧郁症？

sentences.en: How might they be different this year?
sentences.zh: 今年它会有什么不同？

sentences.en: And for those of you who are sad at the thought of a holiday season unlike any other, what can you do to cope this year?
sentences.zh: 对于那些一想到这个与众不同的节日季就感到难过的人，今年你们可以做些什么来应对？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: If you enjoy Speaking of Psychology, the conversation doesn't have to stop when the podcast is over.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢《心理学话你知》，对话并不会在播客结束时停止。

sentences.zh: 只需支付一笔低廉的费用，注册参加美国心理学会2020年虚拟大会，即可无限期访问数百个关于最新心理学进展的视频。

sentences.en: Start with some of our selected videos featuring psychology's biggest names, discussing topics such as COVID-19, racism, and stigma.
sentences.zh: 从我们精选的由心理学大咖主讲的视频开始看起，探讨诸如2019冠状病毒病、种族主义和污名化等话题。

sentences.en: Or let your curiosity take the lead and use our on-demand library to explore any topic.
sentences.zh: 或者让你的好奇心引领方向，利用我们的点播库探索任何你感兴趣的话题。

sentences.en: Go to convention.apa.org slash podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 请访问 convention.apa.org 斜杠 podcaSt。

sentences.en: That's convention.apa.org slash podcaSt.
sentences.zh: That's convention.apa.org slash podcaSt.

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Elaine Rodino, a psychologist in private practice in State College, Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是伊莱恩·罗迪诺博士，她是宾夕法尼亚州州立学院的私人执业心理学家。

sentences.en: She's an APA fellow and a former president of APA's Division of Psychologists in Independent Practice.
sentences.zh: 她是美国心理学会资深会员，也是美国心理学会独立执业心理学家分会的前主席。

sentences.en: She's also had a longstanding interest in the holiday blues and has helped many of her patients with this issue over the years.
sentences.zh: 她长期以来对节日忧郁症很感兴趣，多年来一直在这一问题上帮助了许多患者。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Rodino.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学话你知》，罗迪诺博士。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Good to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Let's start with a broad definition.
sentences.zh: 让我们从一个广泛的定义开始。

sentences.en: What are holiday blues?
sentences.zh: 什么是节日忧郁症？

sentences.en: As I said earlier, there's no actual diagnosis, but is it a real condition and what are its hallmarks?
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才所说，这并没有实际的诊断，但它是一种真实的状况吗？它的特征是什么？

sentences.en: Yes, it is a real condition and I'm really glad you noted that it's not a diagnosable condition.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种真实的状况，我很高兴你指出它不是一种可诊断的状况。

sentences.en: So that it's a condition that usually appears around the holidays and then fades away sometime in January.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种通常在节日期间出现，然后在1月份某个时候逐渐消退的状况。

sentences.en: And what are they?
sentences.zh: 它们到底是什么？

sentences.en: What are these feelings?
sentences.zh: 这些感受究竟是什么？

sentences.en: They could vary.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: To some people, it's a feeling of malaise.
sentences.zh: 对有些人来说，这是一种身体不适感。

sentences.en: They just feel tired.
sentences.zh: 他们就是觉得累。

sentences.en: They can't get to things.
sentences.zh: 什么事都提不起精神去办。

sentences.en: Other people, it's the traditional bah humbug attitude.
sentences.zh: 对其他人来说，则是传统的讨厌节日的态度。

sentences.en: They hate the holidays, can't wait until they're over, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们讨厌过节，恨不得节日快点结束，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And for some people, they're just stressed out.
sentences.zh: 还有些人，他们只是压力山大。

sentences.en: They're like just scattered all over the place and just in a frenzy of needing to do so many things.
sentences.zh: 他们就像无头苍蝇一样焦头烂额，陷入必须要做那么多事情的狂乱之中。

sentences.en: So however this affects people, and for some people, they don't have this at all.
sentences.zh: 所以无论这对人们产生什么影响，有些人其实完全没有这种感觉。

sentences.en: So it's not that you must have one of these conditions.
sentences.zh: 因此，并不是说你一定会有这些状况中的某一种。

sentences.en: And again, it's good to know that they do fade away in January.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，好消息是它们在1月份确实会消退。

sentences.en: How did you first become interested in this topic?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么开始对这个话题感兴趣的？

sentences.en: Ah, that's an interesting story.
sentences.zh: 啊，那是一个有趣的故事。

sentences.en: This was way back when I was an intern in psychology at the Los Angeles Suicide Prevention Center, which, since that time, has now been taken over by the D.D.
sentences.zh: 那是很久以前的事了，当时我在洛杉矶自杀预防中心担任心理学实习生，从那以后，该中心现在已被洛杉矶的D.D.赫希心理健康中心接管。

sentences.en: Hirsch Mental Health Center in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: （接上一句）

sentences.en: Well, the center at that time was the very first suicide prevention center.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时该中心是第一家自杀预防中心。

sentences.en: The leaders there were the ones that created the programs for suicide and suicide hotlines.
sentences.zh: 那里的负责人正是创建自杀干预项目和自杀热线的人。

sentences.en: And the media would very actively come and talk with people, interview us.
sentences.zh: 媒体会非常积极地过来跟我们交流、采访我们。

sentences.en: And that's actually how I also started doing work with media and get comfortable working with the media.
sentences.zh: 这也是我开始与媒体合作并适应与媒体打交道的方式。

sentences.en: Well, they would come every holiday time and want to know, is it true more people commit suicide in December?
sentences.zh: 嗯，每到节日期间，他们就会过来询问：是不是真的有更多人在12月份自杀？

sentences.en: And the response is, no, they don't.
sentences.zh: 而回答是，并没有。

sentences.en: It's not a higher suicide month.
sentences.zh: 这不是自杀率更高的月份。

sentences.en: But what the gurus at the Suicide Prevention Center started to formulate was, and coined the term holiday blues,
sentences.zh: 但自杀预防中心的专家们开始构思并创造了“节日忧郁症”这个词，

sentences.en: that there were these feelings of blues, but not a diagnosable depression or suicidalness.
sentences.zh: 即存在这种忧郁的情绪，但并非可诊断的抑郁症或自杀倾向。

sentences.en: Why do you think that myth persists that there are more suicides around the holidays?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么“节日期间自杀人数更多”这种迷思会一直存在？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's decreased over time, because I've been doing interviews about holiday blues since that time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为随着时间推移这种情况已经减少了，因为从那时起我一直在做关于节日忧郁症的采访。

sentences.en: And I have seen a decrease.
sentences.zh: 我确实看到了减少的趋势。

sentences.en: In fact, I haven't been asked that question in many years.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我已经很多年没被问过这个问题了。

sentences.en: So I think people are now focusing on holiday blues rather than suicide.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为人们现在关注的是节日忧郁症，而不是自杀。

sentences.en: Or they're reading the statistics and they see that it's not actually there, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 或者他们查阅了统计数据，发现情况并非如此，也许吧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you've been a practitioner for a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以你当了很长时间的临床医生。

sentences.en: And is this something that you see commonly in your practice among your patients?
sentences.zh: 在你的执业经历中，在患者群体里，这是常见的情况吗？

sentences.en: Do you see an uptick in blues during the holidays?
sentences.zh: 你是否看到在节日期间忧郁情绪有所上升？

sentences.en: Well, I don't believe I have ever had anyone actually come to therapy because of holiday blues.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不认为我曾遇到过真正因为节日忧郁症而来看心理治疗的人。

sentences.en: But almost all my patients discuss it in their sessions.
sentences.zh: 但几乎我所有的患者都会在会诊时讨论这个话题。

sentences.en: You know, during the holiday time, there's always conversations about how they're going to get through the holidays,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在节日期间，总会有关于他们将如何度过节日、

sentences.en: what they're doing, what the stresses are, how they're going to deal with getting together with family.
sentences.zh: 他们在做什么、压力是什么、他们将如何应对与家人聚会的讨论。

sentences.en: And this year, with the pandemic, it's, you know, totally, you know, another whole layer of issues going on.
sentences.zh: 而今年碰上疫情，你知道的，这完全带来了又一整层的问题。

sentences.en: And by the way, there are fewer issues in some respects, because many people are not doing face-to-face gatherings.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，从某些方面来看，问题反而变少了，因为许多人没有进行面对面的聚会。

sentences.en: So there's a reduction in some of the stress that goes on with that.
sentences.zh: 因此，与之相关的某些压力有所减轻。

sentences.en: So you're hearing that the people, for example, who are afraid to get together with, you know, Uncle Maury,
sentences.zh: 所以你听到有人说，比如那些害怕跟莫里叔叔聚在一起的人，

sentences.en: because we don't agree on politics, you're not going to see Uncle Maury this year.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在政治上意见不合，今年你就不用见莫里叔叔了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But it still comes up because they're worried about Uncle Maury showing up on Zoom.
sentences.zh: 但这个问题还是会出现，因为他们担心莫里叔叔会出现在Zoom视频里。

sentences.en: Don't give him the link.
sentences.zh: 别把链接发给他。

sentences.en: Well, you can always somehow have a technical malfunction and disconnect.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你总是可以用某种方式制造技术故障然后断开连接。

sentences.en: Sorry, I can't hear you.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我听不清你说话。

sentences.en: Well, who is most at risk of getting holiday blues?
sentences.zh: 嗯，谁最容易患上节日忧郁症？

sentences.en: Well, I kind of see there can be some, what you may think of as bad reasons, and you may think of other reasons as good reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我发现其中既有你可能会认为是糟糕原因的因素，也有你可能会认为是良好原因的因素。

sentences.en: I find most of the time, it's related to issues that happened to people earlier in their lives.
sentences.zh: 我发现大多数时候，这与人们早年生活中发生的事情有关。

sentences.en: And under the bad category, the example would be having an alcoholic parent.
sentences.zh: 在糟糕的类别下，一个例子就是有一个酗酒的父母。

sentences.en: Often, an alcoholic parent would have a way of just really ruining a holiday.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，酗酒的父母会有一种方式彻底毁掉一个节日。

sentences.en: You know, as the drinking goes on during the day, they may become hostile, aggressive, and somehow really make an ugly Christmas Day or Thanksgiving Day.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，随着白天酒越喝越多，他们可能会变得充满敌意、好斗，并以某种方式把圣诞节或感恩节过得一团糟。

sentences.en: And, you know, or, you know, kind of the Uncle Maury stories that they remember.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，或者说他们记忆中莫里叔叔的故事。

sentences.en: And that's why those kind of jokes persist, because they did happen.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这类笑话一直存在，因为它们确实发生过。

sentences.en: There could be some pretty hostile family arguments and people storming out.
sentences.zh: 可能会有一些相当充满敌意的家庭争吵，有人气冲冲地夺门而出。

sentences.en: And, you know, I never heard of food fights.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我以前没听说过食物大战。

sentences.en: But, you know, so, and for children, it could be pretty memorable in negative ways.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，所以对孩子们来说，这可能会留下相当深刻的负面记忆。

sentences.en: So, people may feel uncomfortable with holidays without even particularly remembering why.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们在过节时可能会感到不自在，甚至未必记得具体原因。

sentences.en: But they just are uncomfortable with it.
sentences.zh: 但他们就是觉得不舒服。

sentences.en: On the good side, some people have early childhood memories of everything being so perfect.
sentences.zh: 从好的方面来看，有些人对童年早期有着一切都完美无比的记忆。

sentences.en: They had families, you know, maybe their father decorated the house and it was a best, most lit up house in the whole neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 他们有家人，也许他们的父亲把房子装饰了一番，那是整个社区里亮化得最好的房子。

sentences.en: Or, you know, their mother baked 300 cookies and wrapped them beautifully and delivered them to all the neighbors.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，他们的母亲烤了300块曲奇，把它们精美地包装好，送给所有的邻居。

sentences.en: Well, these then get taken on as traditions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些随后就被当作传统延续下来了。

sentences.en: And people feel they need to do that kind of special, over-the-top holiday.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得他们需要做到那种特别的、极致完美的节日氛围。

sentences.en: And, you know, so that can bring a lot of stress.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，所以这会带来很大的压力。

sentences.en: It's the expectations of what they feel, either negative or positive.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们感受到的期望，无论是负面的还是正面的。

sentences.en: So, then for this year, I mean, the people who have those good memories, they may not be able to share them.
sentences.zh: 那么对于今年来说，我是说，那些拥有美好回忆的人，他们可能无法分享这些回忆了。

sentences.en: And what's going to happen to those folks?
sentences.zh: 那些人会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, well, see, even those good memories become problems because it adds to the stress that they feel that they need to follow in those traditions that their parents did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对啊，你看，甚至那些美好的回忆也成了问题，因为它增加了他们的压力，让他们觉得自己必须遵循父母当年的那些传统。

sentences.en: And I always advise people to start their own traditions, either, you know, as yourself or family.
sentences.zh: 我总是建议人们开创自己的传统，无论是以个人的名义还是以家庭的名义。

sentences.en: If people always just follow traditions, my favorite thing to say is, if we never changed and evolved, we would still be celebrating the way they did in the medieval times.
sentences.zh: 如果人们总是墨守成规，我最喜欢说的一句话是：如果我们从不改变和演变，我们现在依然会按照中世纪的方式来庆祝节日。

sentences.en: Things would have never changed.
sentences.zh: 事情将永远不会改变。

sentences.en: So, clearly, people, you know, zig and zag and create new ways of doing things.
sentences.zh: 所以，很显然，人们会转换思路，创造做事的新方式。

sentences.en: So, and this year is, you know, a major change.
sentences.zh: 因此，今年是一个重大的改变。

sentences.en: So, people do need to become creative
sentences.zh: 所以人们确实需要发挥创意，

sentences.en: and think of new ways to celebrate.
sentences.zh: 并想出庆祝的新方法。

sentences.en: Do you have some strategies or your client's asking you or just discussing what you might do instead?
sentences.zh: 你有什么策略吗？或者你的客户会问你，还是只是讨论你可以用什么来替代？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, you know, what I would also advise is just Googling ideas for pandemic holidays.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，你知道的，我也会建议去谷歌搜索一下关于疫情期间过节的点子。

sentences.en: And, in fact, preparing for this interview, I Googled it to see what was there.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在为这次采访做准备时，我搜了一下看看都有什么。

sentences.en: And there are pages of ideas.
sentences.zh: 结果有满满好几页的点子。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's something for everyone.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，总有一款适合每个人。

sentences.en: A survey that we did at APA quite a while ago, it was actually 2006, it found that women were more likely than men to report higher stress during the holidays.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学会很久以前做过的一项调查，其实是在2006年，发现女性比男性更有可能在节日期间报告承受更高的压力。

sentences.en: And I think we theorized that a lot of the work of preparing for these celebrations falls on women.
sentences.zh: 我想我们推测过，筹备这些庆祝活动的大量工作都落在了女性身上。

sentences.en: Does this ring true for you?
sentences.zh: 这符合你的直觉吗？

sentences.en: Is it your experience that women experience the holiday blues more severely or in greater numbers?
sentences.zh: 根据你的经验，女性经历的节日忧郁症是否更严重或人数更多？

sentences.en: Yeah, and no, I don't think I can say statistically in greater numbers, but the issues are different.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也不是，我不认为我能从统计数据上说人数更多，但问题是不同的。

sentences.en: I think the men have more often been concerned about the Uncle Maury situations and the women more worried about the 300 cookies.
sentences.zh: 我认为男性更多时候是在担心莫里叔叔的情况，而女性则更担心那300块曲奇。

sentences.en: So, because, and that would be the doing more.
sentences.zh: 所以，因为，那将意味着要做更多的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, but the, you know, men also would be decorating the house to be the best in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是，你知道的，男性也会把房子装饰成社区里最好看的。

sentences.en: So, for people who are feeling trepidation right now or looking ahead to November and December,
sentences.zh: 因此，对于那些现在感到忐忑不安或在展望11月和12月的人来说，

sentences.en: what would you advise people to do in order to cope, particularly if they're feeling stressed already?
sentences.zh: 你建议人们做些什么来应对，特别是如果他们已经感到压力重重的话？

sentences.en: Well, one thing is realizing that it's time limited.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一件事是意识到它是有时限的。

sentences.en: Another is doing self-care things, you know, making sure you keep up with the usual self-care things that you do, you know, whether it's exercising,
sentences.zh: 另一件是做一些自我关爱的事情，你知道的，确保你坚持日常的自我关爱活动，无论它是锻炼身体、

sentences.en: taking a warm bath, just taking a break and reading a book.
sentences.zh: 泡个热水澡，还是仅仅休息一下读本书。

sentences.en: So there needs to be just some time that you just check out from the holiday stress part.
sentences.zh: 因此，你需要留出一些时间，让自己从节日压力的部分中抽离出来。

sentences.en: So, wearing your therapist hat,
sentences.zh: 那么，戴上你的治疗师帽子，

sentences.en: what about people who were having the holiday blues and feel really bad?
sentences.zh: 对于那些患有节日忧郁症并且感觉非常糟糕的人，你有什么看法？

sentences.en: I mean, how do you know when you're slipping from just basic holiday blues that will go away into something that could be more serious or long-term?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你怎么知道自己是从会消退的单纯节日忧郁症，滑向可能更严重或更长期的状况？

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think it is the two things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是两点决定的。

sentences.en: One is how dysfunctional is it making you during the holiday time?
sentences.zh: 首先是它在节日期间给你造成了多大程度的功能受损？

sentences.en: You know, are you just, you know, staying in bed, pulling the covers over your head, just waiting for the calendar pages to slip by?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你是不是只是躺在床上，把被子拉过头顶，只是在等待日历的页码翻过？

sentences.en: And then the other thing is, how long does it last into January?
sentences.zh: 然后另一件事是，这种情况持续到1月份有多久？

sentences.en: Usually this starts fading the first couple of weeks in January.
sentences.zh: 通常这种情况在1月的前两周开始消退。

sentences.en: So if people are still feeling that by, say, the second, third week of January, then they really should talk with a psychologist because they could be issues
sentences.zh: 所以如果人们到了1月份的第二或第三周仍然有这种感觉，那么他们真的应该跟心理学家聊聊，因为可能存在一些问题

sentences.en: that really need to be sorted out and processed.
sentences.zh: 确实需要被厘清和处理。

sentences.en: Well, speaking of January, so the blues might go away, but then you've made some New Year's resolutions and maybe by the third or fourth week,
sentences.zh: 嗯，说到1月份，忧郁情绪可能会消失，但接着你又许下了新年愿望，也许到了第三或第四周，

sentences.en: you're saying, well, I can't go to the gym and it's really hard to work out at home.
sentences.zh: 你就会说，嗯，我不能去健身房，在家锻炼真的很难。

sentences.en: And I, you know, are people beating themselves up because they're not keeping the resolutions?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，人们是不是因为没有兑现新年愿望而在自我苛责？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's another whole set of issues, right?
sentences.zh: 对，那是另一大堆问题，对吧？

sentences.en: The New Year resolutions, that's actually another podcast you can do.
sentences.zh: 新年愿望，那其实是你可以做的另一个播客主题。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Because there are, you know, tips on, you know, making them reasonable and not have this kind of magical thinking that you're going to become this different person on January 1St.
sentences.zh: 因为这里面有一些小贴士，比如让愿望保持合理，不要抱有那种要在1月1日变成一个完全不同的人的奇思妙想。

sentences.en: Well, I think it would be good maybe to talk a little bit about that now because then people can be prepared, you know, that you start thinking about it in December,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得现在稍微谈谈这个可能挺好的，这样人们就可以做好准备，你知道的，你从12月份就开始考虑这件事，

sentences.en: like, you know, the January 1st is coming.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，1月1日就要来了。

sentences.en: So what are realistic ways of preparing for trying to be better, say, in the new year, but not going over the top?
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么切合实际的方法可以为新年的自我提升做准备，同时又不过度呢？

sentences.en: Well, exactly the way you said it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你所说的那样。

sentences.en: I think it is good to think ahead and think, well, it's a new year, fresh start.
sentences.zh: 我认为提前思考并觉得“好吧，这是新的一年，全新的开始”，这很好。

sentences.en: Hopefully 2021 will be a better year.
sentences.zh: 希望2021年会是更好的一年。

sentences.en: And, you know, what do I want to accomplish?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我想完成什么？

sentences.en: What do I want to do?
sentences.zh: 我想做什么？

sentences.en: And have it be reasonable.
sentences.zh: 并且要切合实际。

sentences.en: Because, you know, as I said before, you are still you.
sentences.zh: 因为，正如我之前所说，你依然是你。

sentences.en: You know, don't think you're suddenly going to be this superhuman being capable of, you know, these grand things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不要以为你突然就会变成那种能够完成宏伟壮举的超人。

sentences.en: You're not going to do an Ironman kind of thing if you don't even take a hike.
sentences.zh: 如果你连徒步都没尝试过，你是不可能去参加铁人三项这种活动的。

sentences.en: And what about you?
sentences.zh: 那你呢？

sentences.en: Do you have some coping strategies that you're working on for this year?
sentences.zh: 你今年有没有在运用什么应对策略？

sentences.en: I think just hoping that we can all get out and socialize again.
sentences.zh: 我想就是希望我们大家都能再次出门社交吧。

sentences.en: But in the meanwhile, in terms of coping strategies, I do a lot of video virtual meetings, you know, aside from my practice being totally virtual, I do socialize a lot.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，在应对策略方面，我做了很多视频虚拟会议，你知道的，除了我的诊疗工作完全是虚拟的之外，我也有很多社交活动。

sentences.en: And I'm so surprised that I almost have to remind myself that I'm not meeting people in person.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶，我几乎不得不提醒自己，我并不是在跟人面对面见面。

sentences.en: So it's really helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So that's a good thing to keep in mind, I think, as we get toward Christmas and you can't go see the grandchildren, but you can Zoom with them.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，当我们临近圣诞节却无法去看望孙辈时，记住这一点很有好处，但你可以通过Zoom和他们视频。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Well, this has been very helpful.
sentences.zh: 好的，这次谈话非常有用。

sentences.en: I hope that a couple of these tips will make people feel better as we get into the holiday season.
sentences.zh: 我希望其中几条建议能让大家在进入节日季时感觉好一些。

sentences.en: So I want to thank you for joining us today, Dr. Rodino.
sentences.zh: 因此，罗迪诺博士，我要感谢你今天加入我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或您获取播客的任何地方收听《心理学热线》往期节目。

sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，请发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 我们的音效剪辑师是克里斯·孔达扬。

sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。
